newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares inch down, seen rebounding.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares inch down, seen rebounding.

text.p: The Polish bourse inched down in stable turnover on Monday but analysts saw it rebounding, pushed by speculative buying before the release of monthly earnings reports due later this week.

The main market's all-share WIG index inched down 27.3 points, or 0.2 percent, to 14,893.1, total turnover amounted to 112.2 million zlotys ($40.1 million) on both markets as 34 issues fell, 32 rose and 13 were flat.
Analysts said the market, currently 1.2 percent below the October 9, 30-month high of 15,078.7 points, should reach that level on expectations of good September earnings reports.

"We should challenge the high this week as the speculation before the release of the reports should buoy some stocks, which in turn could lift the whole market," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Pekao SA brokerage.
Some analysts said the market was likely to lose steam after climbing to recent record highs and could slip to 14,000 or 13,500 points before the end of the year.
They said that if mass privatisation NFI units kept drawing investors from stocks, the latter could suffer.
NFI units fell 1.2 percent on Monday to 163 zlotys in a 30.9-million-zloty ($11 million) turnover.

Analysts said construction company Budimex rose 4.2 percent in four-million-zloty ($1.4 million) trade after it won last week a 188.2-million-zloty ($67.2 million) contract and they saw the stock extending gains.
Shoe firm Ariel started trade on the parallel market at 15 zlotys ($5.3), 11.1 percent above its public offering price.
